doc.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Playing in his father's band and early Quincy orchestras
summary: At ten or eleven he plays in his father's small band, then at twelve joins Monk Huffman's orchestra and the Red Ramblers.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Very good breath control. And his tone quality was superb. And it showed, all of this, on his recordings. Well I would say when I was ten or eleven years old I’d been playing a couple of years on the trombone and I picked things up very quickly as far as jazz is concerned. I was really having a lot of fun learning that kind of music. And even by the time I was ten or eleven years old, I was playing in my father’s orchestra. He had a little orchestra and I would play in this little five or six piece band for different things around Quincy. So I got an early start. And I can recall many days in my schooling days, in grade school, I would go in to school and I would fall asleep in class because the night before I had been playing a dance somewhere.
You say, “Teacher, I had a gig, what can I do?” Did your father pay you?

No I don’t think he really did. But it wasn’t very long after that, I was about twelve years old and I — well the word kind of got around that I was I guess an up-and-coming player in town. So I auditioned with another piano player in town who had an orchestra and he came to my house and I played a few tunes with him and he hired me to play in his orchestra. As a matter of fact you have his first name also, Monk.

Monk Huffman in Quincy, was a piano player. So I started playing with his orchestra. Then another band kind of got the word and well I also started playing with a group called the Red Ramblers Orchestra. And we had a violin and guitar and drums, and bass and piano. I think that was it.
So this music that you were playing at this time, was it somewhat improvised?
